After nearly slipping off the reformer during a single-leg lunge, I decided to finally fix it properly. I’d tried bare feet, cheap multipacks and a couple of boutique-studio brands. Nothing fixed the real problem: grip that only covers part of the sole and socks that don’t stay put.
Then I discovered AURELUNE. With over 67,000 reviews, a 4.9 out of 5 rating and more than 2 million pairs sold, I figured it was worth putting to the test.

The socks arrived quickly, and I was immediately surprised by how soft and substantial they felt – a plush terry footbed underneath, a snug ribbed band around the arch, and grip dots covering the entire sole from heel to toe.

AURELUNE uses a high-traction full-foot silicone grip that anchors your whole foot to reformer carriages, wooden studio floors and yoga mats. That means no sliding during planks and no toe-clenching to hold a position.

But what really sets it apart is how it stays in place. The compression arch band hugs your midfoot so the sock never twists or slides off your heel mid-exercise – and the cushioned terry footbed softens every press against the footbar.
You don’t need to think about your footing anymore, you just pull them on and focus on your practice.
After seeing all the praise, I had to put them to the test myself to see if they truly live up to the hype.
Here’s what I found.
As advertised, AURELUNE fits snugly with no extra fabric bunching under the toes. I wear a US 10 and the M/L fit perfectly.

I wore them for three months of classes: reformer flows, mat Pilates, barre, a few heated sessions and plenty of at-home workouts on hardwood floors. I specifically tested them in the moves where my feet usually slip.

In my first reformer class in them, I held a full plank on the carriage with zero sliding, no readjusting and no toes gripping for dear life. The grip pattern runs right to the tips of the toes, so even long stretch and elephant felt locked in.
The terry footbed made footwork on the bar far more comfortable, and the low scalloped cuff stayed exactly where I put it through every set.
That’s when I knew the full-foot grip was doing exactly what it promised.
Now, let’s talk about durability.
Grip socks take a beating, so I didn’t baby them. They went through sweaty classes several times a week and more trips through the washing machine than I can count.

After all that, the grip dots haven’t peeled or faded, and the arch band still snaps back into place. The heat-bonded silicone and combed cotton blend held up far better than the cheaper pairs I’ve owned. That’s exactly what you need from a sock you trust on a moving carriage.
In the end, AURELUNE passed every test with flying colors. It’s simple, effective, and does exactly what a great grip sock should do.
